topics.name: Variables, Data Types, Operators & Conditionals
topics.desc: Pure grammar rules. Reading MDN or javascript.info covers this in one sitting.

topics.name: Loops, Strings, Built-in Objects & Error Handling
topics.desc: Straightforward iteration and object API. Read and try examples inline.

topics.name: Objects, Arrays, Classes & Default Parameters
topics.desc: Reference type rules are declarative — documentation covers all edge cases clearly.

topics.name: Plain Functions vs Arrow Functions
topics.desc: Key difference: arrow functions do not have their ownthiscontext. Read once, internalize, done.

topics.name: Destructuring, Spread/Rest, Optional Chaining
topics.desc: ES6+ syntax rules. Extremely pattern-based — read the MDN examples and you're set.

topics.name: Array Higher-Order Methods — map, filter, reduce, find, forEach
topics.desc: Functional patterns used constantly in React. Learn the signatures from docs, practice on arrays.

topics.name: How JavaScript Works — Execution Context & Call Stack
topics.desc: You need to see how the JS engine creates Global Execution Context, how variables/functions are hoisted into memory in Phase 1, and how the Call Stack tracks them. Critical foundation for everything that follows.

links.text: ▶ Namaste JS Ep.1 — How JS Works & Execution Context

topics.name: Hoisting in JavaScript — Variable & Function Hoisting
topics.desc: Understanding whyvargivesundefinedand functions are available before declaration requires seeing memory allocation happen before execution starts.

topics.name: Scope Chain, Lexical Environment & Temporal Dead Zone
topics.desc: How nested functions look up variables through lexical environments. TDZ forlet/constrequires visualizing the memory block before initialization.

links.text: ▶ Namaste JS Ep.7 — Scope & Lexical Environment
▶ Namaste JS Ep.8 — let & const, TDZ

topics.name: Closures — Deep Dive
topics.desc: One of the most important interview topics. A closure "closes over" its outer lexical environment — you need to see the memory snapshot visually to understand why the reference persists even after the outer function returns.

links.text: ▶ Namaste JS Ep.11 — setTimeout + Closures Interview Qs

topics.name: Object Cloning (Shallow vs Deep) & Garbage Collection
topics.desc: Seeing stack vs heap reference diagrams during shallow/deep clone is critical. Understanding when reference counts drop to zero for GC is a runtime concept.

topics.name: thisKeyword — All Behaviors
topics.desc: The most confusing JS concept becausethischanges based on how a function is called, not where it's defined. Seeing call-site diagrams makes the rules stick. Common SDE interview question.

topics.name: DOM Access, Traversal & Manipulation — createElement, querySelector, innerHTML
topics.desc: These are API method lookups. Read MDN, try each method in browser console. Build a small to-do list to cement them.

topics.name: Styling Elements via JS — classList, style, getComputedStyle
topics.desc: Straightforward API — read the MDN reference and use the console to experiment.

topics.name: Event Loop, Web APIs, Microtask Queue & Callback Queue
topics.desc: Most asked JS interview topic.You need to watch a step-by-step tracer showing how setTimeout, Promises, and fetch interact with the Call Stack, Web APIs, Microtask Queue, and Callback Queue. No diagram in a book matches seeing it animate live.

topics.name: Events, addEventListener, Event Delegation & Bubbling/Capturing
topics.desc: How an event travels down (capture) and up (bubble) the DOM tree is a spatial concept — watching a tree diagram with the event highlighted at each node is far more effective than reading prose.

topics.name: Browser Rendering — Reflow & Repaint (Performance)
topics.desc: Modifying layout-affecting CSS properties triggers reflow — the browser recalculates geometry for all affected elements. Seeing which CSS properties trigger reflow vs repaint vs compositor-only is a visual performance concept asked in SDE interviews.

topics.name: Callbacks & Callback Hell
topics.desc: Understanding why deeply nested callbacks became a problem sets up the motivation for Promises. Namaste JS shows this progressively.

topics.name: Promises — Creation, Chaining, Error Handling
topics.desc: You need to see a Promise's state machine (pending → fulfilled / rejected) and how.then()chains pass resolved values forward. The mental model is critical before writing async code.

topics.name: Promise APIs — Promise.all, Promise.allSettled, Promise.race, Promise.any
topics.desc: Interview favorites. Each API resolves/rejects at a different point — seeing timeline diagrams of 3 concurrent promises is the clearest way to distinguish them.

topics.name: async / await & Error Handling with try/catch
topics.desc: Understanding howawaitpauses execution inside the async function without blocking the main thread requires grounding in the Event Loop from Phase 2.

topics.name: Fetch API & Making Network Requests
topics.desc: Combinefetchwith async/await and see how a real HTTP response is consumed. Build a small API-calling script while watching.

topics.name: Basic Types — string, number, boolean, any, unknown, never, void
topics.desc: Pure type annotations — exactly the kind of declarative rule you can absorb from docs in an hour.

topics.name: Type Aliases vs Interfaces — when to use each
topics.desc: The distinction (interfaces are open/extendable; type aliases are closed/composable) is a single reference decision. Read the handbook section, bookmark the table.

links.text: ↗ TS Handbook — Type Aliases vs Interfaces

topics.name: Union & Intersection Types, Literal Types, Type Narrowing
topics.desc: Logical type composition with operators (|and&) — directly readable from docs.

topics.name: Generics
topics.desc: Essential for typed utility functions and React hooks. The handbook examples are excellent — read them and write a typed identity function, a typed array wrapper, and a typed API fetch wrapper.

topics.name: Enums, Tuples, Readonly, Partial, Required, Pick, Omit
topics.desc: Utility types used heavily in React and API layers. Each is a one-liner rule — the docs cover all of them on a single page.

topics.name: TypeScript with Functions — typed params, return types, overloads
topics.desc: Straightforward extension of function syntax from JS. Read and apply immediately to the functions you already write.

topics.name: JSX, Components, Props & Event Handling
topics.desc: JSX is syntactic sugar overReact.createElement— pure transformation rules you can read. The new React docs Quick Start is one of the best introductions written.

topics.name: Conditional Rendering & List Rendering
topics.desc: Ternary, short-circuit, and array map patterns — declarative rules readable in 20 minutes.

topics.name: Tailwind CSS
topics.desc: Pure utility-class lookup. Open Tailwind docs alongside your editor — search for the property you want and apply. No video needed.

topics.name: React Hook Form
topics.desc: Excellent getting-started guide — the library is designed around a readable API. Build one form with validation while reading.

topics.name: useState — State Updates, Batching & State Lifting
topics.desc: State updates are asynchronous and batched. You need to see re-render triggers, why stale closures happen, and how lifting state propagates changes down a component tree. Watching Mohit Garg's React series covers this architecturally.

topics.name: useEffect — Side Effects, Dependency Array & Cleanup
topics.desc: The dependency array rules and cleanup function pattern require seeing examples of memory leaks (missing cleanup on timers/subscriptions) and infinite loops (wrong deps) to understand why the rules exist.

topics.name: useContext — Context API & Provider Pattern
topics.desc: Understanding the Provider tree and why components re-render when context value changes is a structural concept — watching a provider wrap diagram is clearer than reading prose.

topics.name: React Router — Routes, Dynamic Segments, Nested Routes, useNavigate
topics.desc: Routing in SPAs requires understanding how the URL maps to component trees without page reloads. Watching a build is faster than assembling this from docs alone.

topics.name: useRef, useMemo & useCallback — Performance Hooks
topics.desc: Top interview hooks.useMemocaches computed values,useCallbackcaches function definitions — both prevent unnecessary child re-renders. Seeing a before/after render-count comparison makes the purpose clear immediately.

topics.name: useReducer — Complex State Management
topics.desc: Bridges the gap betweenuseStateand Redux — seeing action → reducer → state flow visually makes Redux much easier to learn afterward.

topics.name: Redux Toolkit — Store, Slices, Actions, Selectors
topics.desc: Uni-directional data flow (Action → Reducer → Store → UI) is an architectural concept. Watching a diagram showing how dispatched actions flow through the store and trigger re-renders is significantly clearer than reading docs alone.

topics.name: How the Web Works — HTTP, DNS, Client-Server Model
topics.desc: Foundational concepts with clear explanations available in MDN articles. Read once, know forever.

topics.name: HTTP Methods, Status Codes & REST Principles
topics.desc: All reference material — use a cheat sheet while building your first API.

topics.name: Express — Routing, Route Params, Query Strings, Request/Response
topics.desc: Express routing is extremely declarative. Read the getting-started guide and build a simple CRUD API while reading.

topics.name: Error Handling in Express — Custom Error Classes, Error Middleware
topics.desc: The 4-argument error middleware pattern is a specific Express convention. Read it, implement a global error handler, done.

topics.name: Environment Variables — dotenv, config management
topics.desc: Simple pattern — read the dotenv README, configure once, use everywhere.

topics.name: Node.js Architecture — Libuv, Event Loop, Thread Pool, Non-blocking I/O
topics.desc: Understanding why Node can handle thousands of concurrent requests with a single thread requires visualizing the Libuv thread pool, the event loop phases (timers, I/O, close callbacks), and how async file/network I/O offloads to the OS. Critical for backend SDE questions. Follow Mohit Garg's Node playlist.

topics.name: Middlewares in Express — Chain, Order, next(), Custom Middleware
topics.desc: The request-response pipeline is a linear chain of functions — watching how a request moves through authentication → validation → rate-limiter → handler middleware is a visual pipeline concept.

topics.name: Authentication — JWT (Access + Refresh Tokens), Cookie-based Auth
topics.desc: The token lifecycle (sign → send → store → attach to requests → verify → refresh) is a sequence diagram that is much easier to understand visually. This is asked in every full-stack SDE round.

topics.name: File Uploads — Multer, Cloudinary Integration
topics.desc: Multipart form data, how Multer intercepts it, and then streaming the buffer to Cloudinary involves understanding request lifecycle at a deeper level. Follow Mohit Garg's Node playlist for this.

topics.name: MongoDB Setup — Atlas Cloud, Local, Compass GUI
topics.desc: Follow the Atlas getting-started guide — it's a wizard-based setup. No video needed for account creation and cluster configuration.

topics.name: Mongoose Schemas, Models, CRUD Operations
topics.desc: Schema definition with Mongoose is declarative — read the docs and define a few models. The CRUD methods are standard API calls.

topics.name: Mongoose Validators, Middleware (pre/post hooks), Virtual Fields
topics.desc: Pre/post hooks are lifecycle callbacks defined on the schema — the pattern is clear from the docs.

topics.name: Mongoose populate, References & Document Relationships
topics.desc: Understanding howpopulate()joins documents across collections and when to embed vs reference is an architectural decision best seen in a real schema design walkthrough. Watch within Mohit Garg's Node playlist.

topics.name: MVC Architecture — Model, Controller, Router folder structure
topics.desc: Seeing how a codebase gets organized under MVC (routes → controllers → services → models) is a structural decision that watching a project refactor makes much clearer than reading about it.

topics.name: Aggregation Pipeline — $match, $group, $lookup, $project
topics.desc: MongoDB aggregation is a data transformation pipeline — each stage modifies the document stream. Seeing a pipeline diagram with data flowing through stages is significantly clearer than the docs alone.

topics.name: App Router File Structure — page.tsx, layout.tsx, loading.tsx, error.tsx
topics.desc: Folder-based routing conventions are pure rules — read the Next.js docs routing section once and the pattern becomes clear. Each file name has a fixed role.

topics.name: Link Component, useRouter, usePathname, useSearchParams
topics.desc: Client-side navigation API — declarative usage documented clearly. Read and apply.

topics.name: Image Optimization Component — next/image
topics.desc: Declarative props-based API — straightforward docs, takes 15 minutes to learn.

topics.name: API Routes — Route Handlers (GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE)
topics.desc: Next.js Route Handlers replace Express for simple APIs. The pattern is a named export function — read the docs and build a sample CRUD handler.

topics.name: Environment Variables in Next.js — NEXT_PUBLIC prefix rules
topics.desc: Simple naming convention. Read the docs page once.

topics.name: Middleware — matcher config, redirect/rewrite logic
topics.desc: Request-time middleware with a matcher config — readable from the docs reference.

topics.name: Server Components vs Client Components — When to use each
topics.desc: Core Next.js concept.Understanding which components render on the server (no JS sent to client, can access DB directly) vs client (interactive, hooks work) requires seeing a component tree diagram with the rendering boundary marked. The wrong mental model leads to bugs that are hard to debug without this foundation.

topics.name: Data Fetching — Server Components fetch, caching, revalidation
topics.desc: Next.js extends nativefetchwith cache and revalidation options. Understanding howforce-cache,no-store, andrevalidate: Naffect what's rendered and when requires seeing a request timeline. Follow Mohit Garg's playlist.

topics.name: Static Generation (SSG), Server-Side Rendering (SSR) & ISR
topics.desc: The three rendering modes (build-time static, request-time server, incremental background regeneration) are best understood through a timeline diagram showing when each page is rendered. Critical for senior SDE architecture discussions.

topics.name: Server Actions — Form mutations without API routes
topics.desc: Server Actions run on the server but are called from client components — the invocation model blurs the client-server boundary in a way that benefits from watching a demo of the request lifecycle.

topics.name: NextAuth.js (Auth.js) — OAuth, Credentials Provider, Session Management
topics.desc: Authentication setup with multiple providers, session strategy (JWT vs database), and route protection in middleware — an end-to-end flow that is much easier to follow in a video than assembling from the docs.

topics.name: WebSocket Protocol Basics — ws:// handshake, frames, full-duplex
topics.desc: The HTTP Upgrade handshake and why WebSocket is different from polling — read MDN's WebSocket guide. One clear page explains the protocol.

topics.name: Socket.IO — emit, on, rooms, namespaces, broadcast
topics.desc: Socket.IO's event API is declarative — read the Getting Started and Rooms docs. Building a simple chat while reading is enough to understand emit/on semantics.

topics.name: WebSocket Connection Lifecycle & Scaling with Redis Adapter
topics.desc: When multiple Node instances run behind a load balancer, a user's WebSocket connection is on one server while another user is on a different server. Seeing how the Redis pub/sub adapter broadcasts events across all instances is a system design concept that requires an architecture diagram — directly relevant to your chess platform.

topics.name: Real-time Chess Platform Architecture — Game State Sync
topics.desc: Your resume lists a chess platform. Design and implement: room-per-game with 2 socket connections, server-authoritative game state validation (never trust the client for moves), broadcasting state to both players, reconnection handling, and spectator mode. Follow a real-time game tutorial for the pattern.

topics.name: CORS — How it works, preflight, allowed origins in Express
topics.desc: CORS is a browser security mechanism with clear header-based rules. Read MDN's CORS guide once — configure thecorsnpm package while reading.

topics.name: Rate Limiting, Helmet, Input Validation (Zod / Joi)
topics.desc: These are Express middleware packages with clear npm README setups — read and configure. Zod is especially important if you're using TypeScript.

topics.name: Password Hashing — bcrypt, salt rounds
topics.desc: Simple one-way hashing API — read the bcrypt npm README. Understand why plaintext passwords in DB = immediate disqualification in any code review.

topics.name: Caching Concepts — Cache-Control headers, Redis basics
topics.desc: HTTP caching headers are declarative rules. Redis commands for get/set/expire are a clean CLI reference. Read both docs.

topics.name: OAuth 2.0 Flow — Authorization Code Grant, Access Token, Refresh Token
topics.desc: The three-party handshake (client → auth server → resource server) with redirect URIs, authorization codes, and token exchange is a sequence diagram that is nearly impossible to understand without seeing it flow visually. Asked in almost every SDE interview for full-stack roles.

topics.name: Microservices vs Monolith — Trade-offs, Service Communication
topics.desc: Architectural trade-offs and how services communicate (REST, gRPC, message queues) benefit from watching system design videos. This is a standard SDE interview topic at mid-to-senior level.

topics.name: Database Design — Indexing, Query Optimization, Sharding
topics.desc: Index anatomy (B-tree), how compound indexes are traversed, and sharding key selection are data structure concepts best explained with visual tree diagrams. You will be asked to optimize a slow query in technical rounds.

topics.name: CI/CD Pipeline — GitHub Actions, Build → Test → Deploy
topics.desc: Setting up automated pipelines is a visual workflow — seeing how a push triggers a workflow file that runs jobs in sequence/parallel makes the YAML structure make much more sense than reading it cold.

topics.name: Advanced Comprehensions & Generator Expressions
topics.desc: List, dict, set comprehensions are pure syntax rules. Generator expressions (yield, lazy evaluation) are equally declarative — reading Real Python's guide while writing examples is faster than any video.

topics.name: Decorators — Writing Custom Wrappers withfunctools.wraps
topics.desc: Decorators are a function-wrapping pattern (@time_it,@authenticated,@cached) directly readable from the docs. Understand how*args/**kwargsforwarding preserves the original signature. Used constantly in Flask and FastAPI route definitions.

topics.name: Context Managers —with,__enter__/__exit__,contextlib
topics.desc: The protocol is a two-method contract — read it, implement a custom file/DB connection manager. Used for managing GPU memory context and database session scopes in production ML APIs.

topics.name: OOP & Dunder Methods —__init__,__call__,__repr__,__len__,__iter__
topics.desc: __call__is critical for PyTorch — everynn.Modulesubclass runs inference by calling the object like a function.__iter__/__next__are needed for writing custom DataLoaders. Read Real Python's operator overloading guide.

topics.name: Type Hints —typingmodule,Optional,Union,List,Dict, Generics
topics.desc: Type hints are pure syntax annotations. Required for FastAPI — Pydantic reads them at runtime to validate request payloads. Read the mypy docs and the FastAPI typing introduction back-to-back.

topics.name: Exception Handling — Custom Exception Classes, Exception Chaining
topics.desc: Building a hierarchy of domain-specific exceptions (ModelLoadError,InferenceTimeoutError) is a production pattern. Read the docs, implement a custom exception class tree for a mock ML API.

topics.name: Dataclasses & Named Tuples — Lightweight Structured Data
topics.desc: Declarative data containers used for passing structured results between ML pipeline stages. The@dataclassdecorator rules are entirely readable from the docs.

topics.name: The Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) — Why Python Cannot Truly Multithread
topics.desc: The GIL is a CPython-level mutex that prevents multiple threads from executing Python bytecode simultaneously. You must see a diagram of thread contention at the GIL boundary to understand why CPU-bound ML workloads (model inference, matrix multiplication) must usemultiprocessing, notthreading. This is asked directly in production SDE interviews.

links.text: ↗ Real Python — The Python GIL (read alongside video)

topics.name: Python Concurrency — threading vs multiprocessing vs asyncio — When to Use Each
topics.desc: Three different concurrency models for three different bottlenecks:threadingfor I/O-bound (DB reads, API calls),multiprocessingfor CPU-bound (model inference, image decoding),asynciofor async I/O in FastAPI. Seeing a decision tree diagram of which to use and why is essential — getting this wrong in production causes either dead locks or the event loop blocking.

topics.name: Python Memory Management — Reference Counting, Cyclic GC, Memory Profiling
topics.desc: When loading 2GB model weights into RAM, understanding how Python tracks object lifetimes (reference counts), handles circular references (generational GC), and whendel+gc.collect()actually frees memory is critical. You need to see the object lifecycle diagram — a memory leak in a long-running FastAPI server serving ML models is a production-critical bug.

links.text: ↗ Real Python — Python Memory Management (read alongside)

topics.name: asyncio — Event Loop, Coroutines,async def,await, Tasks, Gather
topics.desc: FastAPI is built on asyncio. Watching a visual tracer of how coroutines suspend atawaitand yield control back to the event loop — while the I/O completes in the background — is the exact same mental model as the JS Event Loop from your Node roadmap. Once you see the diagram, FastAPI's async patterns become immediately clear.

topics.name: NumPy — Arrays, Shapes, Dtype, Broadcasting Rules
topics.desc: The broadcasting rules (how arrays of different shapes align for operations) are a set of fixed rules — read the NumPy quickstart, trace through the shape diagrams. This is the foundation of every ML framework's tensor API.

topics.name: NumPy Vectorization — Avoid Python Loops, Use Array Operations
topics.desc: Replacing Pythonforloops with NumPy array operations is the single biggest performance lever in ML data pipelines. The principle is simple — read the docs and benchmark a loop vs vectorized version yourself.

topics.name: NumPy Linear Algebra —dot,matmul,transpose,reshape,einsum
topics.desc: These are API lookups — reference the docs when you need them. The key operations (matrix multiply, transpose, reshape) are used constantly in model implementations. Knoweinsumfor attention mechanism implementations.

topics.name: Pandas — DataFrames, Series, Read CSV/JSON, GroupBy, Merge, Apply
topics.desc: Pandas is a declarative data manipulation API. Read the 10-minutes-to-pandas guide while cleaning a real dataset. Column selection, filtering, and groupby are all straightforward method lookups.

topics.name: Matplotlib & Seaborn — Plotting Loss Curves, Confusion Matrices, Feature Distributions
topics.desc: Visualization APIs — read the gallery examples and adapt them. You'll use these for every ML experiment to plot training/validation loss curves and model evaluation metrics.

topics.name: NumPy Memory Layout — C-contiguous vs F-contiguous, Strides
topics.desc: Understanding how NumPy arrays are laid out in memory (strides — how many bytes to skip to get the next element in each dimension) explains why certain reshape and transpose operations are free (view) while others require a data copy. This affects ML pipeline performance significantly when moving data between CPU and GPU.

topics.name: Flask — Routing, Blueprints, Request Context,jsonify, Error Handlers
topics.desc: Flask is a micro-framework with a small, readable API surface. Build a model-serving endpoint while reading the official docs. Focus on the Application Factory pattern (create_app()) for production structuring.

topics.name: FastAPI — Path Operations, Path/Query Parameters, Response Models
topics.desc: FastAPI's route declaration syntax is clean and declarative — type annotations do the heavy lifting. Read the tutorial start-to-finish while building a simple prediction endpoint.

topics.name: Pydantic V2 — BaseModel, Field validators, nested schemas,model_validator
topics.desc: Pydantic validates incoming request payloads against your type-annotated schemas before they touch your ML pipeline. This catches malformed inputs (wrong shape, wrong dtype cues) at the API boundary — exactly where you want to fail fast. The docs are excellent.

topics.name: FastAPI Background Tasks &HTTPException
topics.desc: Background tasks (fire-and-forget logging, cleanup jobs) and structured HTTP exceptions are simple FastAPI patterns fully covered in the docs.

topics.name: SQLAlchemy (Async) with FastAPI — Session management, async engine
topics.desc: Database access in async FastAPI requires async SQLAlchemy sessions. The pattern is documented clearly — configure an async engine, useAsyncSessionwith dependency injection.

topics.name: WSGI vs ASGI — Flask's Sequential Model vs FastAPI's Async Event Loop
topics.desc: Premier SDE interview topic.Flask (WSGI) handles requests sequentially — each request blocks a thread until it completes. FastAPI (ASGI) uses an async event loop — a request awaiting a DB response suspends and yields the thread to handle another request. Seeing a concurrency diagram of 100 simultaneous requests under each model shows immediately why ASGI crushes WSGI for ML API throughput.

topics.name: FastAPI Dependency Injection —Depends(), Lifespan, Model Loading
topics.desc: Dependency injection in FastAPI controls how expensive resources (ML model instances, DB sessions, auth state) are instantiated and shared across route handlers. The injection tree — which dependencies depend on which — is an architectural diagram. A wrong DI setup causes a 2GB model to reload on every request instead of once on startup.

topics.name: FastAPI Lifespan — Loading ML Models Once on Startup
topics.desc: The@asynccontextmanagerlifespan pattern replaces deprecated@app.on_event("startup"). This is where you load your PyTorch model weights once into shared application state — not inside each request handler. Watch a video showing the memory difference between per-request vs startup loading.

topics.name: Estimator API —fit(),predict(),transform(),fit_transform()
topics.desc: The consistent estimator interface is one of scikit-learn's strengths. Learn it once — every algorithm in the library follows the same contract. Read the API reference, use a linear regression and a random forest to cement the pattern.

topics.name: Supervised Learning — Linear/Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forest, SVM, KNN
topics.desc: For each algorithm, read the scikit-learn user guide section. Focus on hyperparameters and when each algorithm performs well vs poorly — this is what SDE interviews ask about.

topics.name: Preprocessing — StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler, LabelEncoder, OneHotEncoder, Imputer
topics.desc: Feature scaling and encoding rules are fully documented with examples. Read and apply to a real dataset. A common interview mistake is scaling test data with test statistics instead of train statistics — the docs explain why Pipeline prevents this.

topics.name: Pipelines — Chaining Preprocessing + Model, Preventing Data Leakage
topics.desc: Scikit-learn Pipelines ensure transformers are fit only on training data and applied consistently to test data. This is a production best practice — read the Pipeline docs and build one that scales → encodes → trains in one object.

topics.name: Model Evaluation — Cross-validation, Confusion Matrix, ROC-AUC, Precision/Recall
topics.desc: All metric computation is documented with examples in the model evaluation guide. Know why accuracy is misleading for imbalanced classes — use F1, ROC-AUC instead. Interviewers ask this.

topics.name: Hyperparameter Tuning — GridSearchCV, RandomizedSearchCV
topics.desc: Grid and random search are declarative parameter grid definitions combined with cross-validation — entirely readable from the docs.

topics.name: PyTorch Tensors — Creation, Indexing, Slicing, Shape Operations
topics.desc: Tensor API mirrors NumPy — if you know NumPy well, read the PyTorch quickstart to map equivalent operations. Focus on.view()vs.reshape()and why.contiguous()is sometimes required.

topics.name: Dataset & DataLoader — Custom__getitem__, batching, shuffling,num_workers
topics.desc: TheDataset/DataLoaderAPI is declarative — inheritDataset, implement__len__and__getitem__, wrap inDataLoader. This is where your__dunder__knowledge from Phase 1 becomes directly applicable.

topics.name: Loss Functions & Optimizers —CrossEntropyLoss,MSELoss,Adam,SGD,lr_scheduler
topics.desc: These are configuration choices with documented parameters. Read each one, understand what it minimizes, and know the Adam vs SGD trade-off (Adam converges faster, SGD generalizes slightly better).

topics.name: Model Saving & Loading —state_dict,torch.save,torch.load,map_location
topics.desc: The state_dict pattern is a standard documented convention. Know the difference between saving the full model vs state_dict only (always prefer state_dict in production).

topics.name: PyTorch Autograd — Computational Graphs, Forward Pass, Backpropagation
topics.desc: Autograd dynamically builds a computation graph during the forward pass and traverses it in reverse during.backward()to compute gradients. You must see this graph being built and traversed visually — how gradient tensors flow backwards through matrix multiplication nodes is a diagram concept, not a prose concept. Every ML SDE interview probes this.

topics.name: Customnn.Module—__init__,forward(), Subclassing Layers
topics.desc: Every custom model architecture subclassesnn.Moduleand overridesforward(). Watching walkthroughs of a custom CNN, MLP, and attention block — tracking input/output tensor shapes through each layer — cements the architecture patterns you'll use to build every model on your resume.

topics.name: GPU Execution —.to('cuda'),torch.cuda.empty_cache(), Mixed Precision (torch.amp)
topics.desc: Moving tensors and models to CUDA, managing GPU memory (VRAM OOM errors are the #1 production issue in DL), and using automatic mixed precision (FP16 for speed, FP32 for stability) are GPU memory management concepts that require visual diagrams of device memory allocation.

topics.name: Training Loop — Train/Eval Mode, Gradient Zeroing, Gradient Clipping
topics.desc: The canonical PyTorch training loop (zero_grad → forward → loss → backward → step) must be internalized. Watch a loop implementation that explains why each step is in that order — forgettingzero_grad()accumulates gradients incorrectly, and forgettingmodel.eval()leaves BatchNorm/Dropout active during inference.

topics.name: Transfer Learning — Loading Pretrained Weights, Freezing Layers, Fine-tuning
topics.desc: Loading ResNet or ViT pretrained weights, freezing backbone layers, and training only the classification head is an architectural pattern relevant to your CV/YOLO work. Seeing which layer groups get frozen in a diagram vs which remain trainable is essential.

topics.name: Keras Sequential API — Stacking Layers,compile(),fit(),evaluate()
topics.desc: The Sequential API is intentionally high-level and readable. Go through the TensorFlow beginner tutorial while building a model. The declarative layer-stacking syntax maps naturally from reading docs.

topics.name: Keras Functional API — Multi-input/output Models, Shared Layers
topics.desc: The Functional API uses explicit tensor chaining syntax — clearly documented with examples. Use it for any architecture that isn't a simple linear stack.

topics.name: Callbacks — EarlyStopping, ModelCheckpoint, TensorBoard, ReduceLROnPlateau
topics.desc: Training callbacks are configuration objects — documented with all parameters. These are essential for responsible training (saving best weights, stopping early to prevent overfitting).

topics.name: SavedModel Format,model.save(),tf.saved_modelfor Deployment
topics.desc: SavedModel is TF's production serialization format — used by TF Serving and TFLite. Read the docs to understand the difference between SavedModel and the older HDF5.h5format.

topics.name: Custom Training Loop withtf.GradientTape
topics.desc: When you need finer control thanmodel.fit()(e.g., GANs, custom loss functions, gradient surgery), you usetf.GradientTapeto manually record operations and compute gradients. This is TF's equivalent to PyTorch's autograd — watching it trace a forward pass visually reveals how the tape records the computation graph.

topics.name: Subclassingtf.keras.Modelfor Custom Architectures
topics.desc: The PyTorch-style OOP model subclassing pattern is available in TF viatf.keras.Model. Watching a walkthrough of building a Transformer encoder block by subclassing shows the shape transformation tracking that makes custom architectures debuggable.

topics.name: NLP Fundamentals — Tokenization, Embeddings, Vocabulary, Padding, Attention Masks
topics.desc: These are definitional concepts with clear explanations in the Hugging Face NLP course. Read Chapter 1-3 of the HF NLP course — the best free NLP fundamentals resource available.

topics.name: Hugging Facepipeline()— Text Classification, NER, QA, Summarization, Translation
topics.desc: Thepipeline()abstraction is a clean high-level API. Read the docs while running each task type on example inputs. Understandtask=,model=,tokenizer=parameters — this is where your resume's NLP work lives at the surface level.

topics.name: AutoTokenizer & AutoModel — Loading from Hub, Tokenizer Output,input_ids,attention_mask
topics.desc: TheAutoClasspattern is declarative — load by model name string. Understanding tokenizer output keys (input_ids,attention_mask,token_type_ids) is reference material from the docs.

topics.name: Hugging FacedatasetsLibrary — Loading, Mapping, Filtering, Batching
topics.desc: The datasets library has a cleanmap()-based transformation API. Read the guide — it processes data in Apache Arrow format, which is faster than pandas for large NLP datasets.

links.text: ↗ HF Datasets — Use a Dataset Guide

topics.name: Hugging FaceTrainerAPI —TrainingArguments, Compute Metrics, Fine-tuning Flow
topics.desc: TheTrainerabstracts the training loop. Read the fine-tuning guide while fine-tuning a BERT model on a classification task — this maps directly to your NLP project resume items.

topics.name: Transformer Architecture — Self-Attention, Multi-Head Attention, Positional Encoding
topics.desc: Essential for any NLP SDE role.The query/key/value dot-product attention mechanism, how multiple attention heads focus on different semantic relationships simultaneously, and how positional encodings inject sequence order into a permutation-invariant architecture — all require visual animated diagrams. "Attention Is All You Need" is much easier to understand after watching a visual walkthrough.

links.text: ▶ Andrej Karpathy — Let's build GPT from scratch

topics.name: BERT vs GPT vs T5 — Encoder-only, Decoder-only, Encoder-Decoder Architectures
topics.desc: Understanding which architecture to choose for which task (BERT for understanding/classification, GPT for generation, T5 for seq2seq) requires seeing the masked attention patterns and token flow diagrams for each. Interviewers ask why you'd use BERT over GPT for text classification.

topics.name: Tokenization Deep Dive — BPE, WordPiece, SentencePiece
topics.desc: Understanding how subword tokenization algorithms build vocabularies (and why "unhappiness" → ["un", "##happin", "##ess"]) requires seeing the merge step visualizations. This explains vocabulary size vs OOV trade-offs asked in NLP interviews.

topics.name: LangChain LCEL — Chain Primitives,RunnableSequence,RunnableParallel
topics.desc: LangChain Expression Language is a declarative pipe-based composition syntax (prompt | llm | output_parser). Read the LCEL docs — the syntax is clean enough to learn directly from the reference.

topics.name: Prompt Templates —ChatPromptTemplate, System/Human/AI message roles
topics.desc: Template construction is declarative — read the docs and build a few prompt templates with variable injection. Know the role system (system, human, ai) used by all major LLM APIs.

topics.name: Document Loaders & Text Splitters —RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter, chunk size, overlap
topics.desc: Document loading and chunking strategies are configuration choices with documented parameters. Understand why chunk overlap exists (preserving context across boundaries) — this is a RAG design question interviewers ask.

topics.name: Vector Stores — Chroma, FAISS, pgvector — Indexing and Similarity Search
topics.desc: Vector store operations (add_documents,similarity_search) are clean API calls. Read the LangChain vector store integration docs and the FAISS getting-started guide — understand cosine similarity vs dot product as retrieval metrics.

topics.name: LangChain Tools — Defining Custom Tools,@tooldecorator, Tool Schema
topics.desc: Tool definitions are function + docstring + schema — declarative and documented. Understand how an LLM reads the tool schema to decide which tool to call.

topics.name: Advanced RAG Pipeline — Chunking Strategies, Embedding, Retrieval, Reranking, Prompt Synthesis
topics.desc: A production RAG system involves: document chunking (fixed-size, semantic, hierarchical) → embedding generation (sentence-transformers, OpenAI embeddings) → vector index storage → similarity search (top-k retrieval) → optional cross-encoder reranking → context injection into prompt → LLM generation. This is an end-to-end system diagram that requires a video walkthrough — directly tied to your PDF Query Engine project.

topics.name: Embeddings — What They Are, Why Cosine Similarity Works, Embedding Models
topics.desc: Understanding why semantically similar text lands close in 768-dimensional vector space — and why cosine similarity measures the angle (not distance) — requires seeing visualized 2D projections of high-dimensional embedding clusters. This is asked in every GenAI SDE interview.

topics.name: LangGraph / LangChain Agents — ReAct Pattern, Tool Calling Loop, State Management
topics.desc: Multi-agent systems using the ReAct (Reason + Act) pattern — where the LLM decides which tool to call, gets the result, reasons about it, and decides the next action — is a loop architecture that benefits enormously from watching a step-by-step trace of thought → action → observation → thought. Critical for your PDF Query Engine architecture explanation in interviews.

topics.name: LLM Fine-tuning — LoRA / QLoRA, PEFT, Parameter-Efficient Methods
topics.desc: Full fine-tuning of a 7B model requires 100+ GB VRAM. LoRA injects low-rank adapter matrices into attention layers and trains only those — reducing trainable parameters by 99%. Seeing which weight matrices get the low-rank injection and why it works is a visual linear algebra concept asked in advanced ML SDE rounds.

topics.name: Docker for ML — Dockerfile for Python/PyTorch, GPU passthrough, Multi-stage Builds
topics.desc: Container definitions are declarative Dockerfile instructions. Read the Docker Python guide and the NVIDIA container toolkit docs — getting--gpus allworking is a known setup pattern.

topics.name: MLflow — Experiment Tracking,log_metric,log_param, Model Registry
topics.desc: MLflow's logging API is a few function calls — declarative and well-documented. Integrate it into any training loop in 10 lines.

topics.name: Model Quantization — INT8, FP16, ONNX Export for Faster Inference
topics.desc: Converting a FP32 model to INT8 reduces size by 4x and inference latency by 2-3x. Read the PyTorch quantization docs and the Optimum library for HF model quantization.

topics.name: Uvicorn + Gunicorn — Production ASGI Deployment, Worker Configuration
topics.desc: The production FastAPI deployment pattern (Gunicorn as process manager, Uvicorn as ASGI worker) is documented clearly. Know the worker count formula (2 × CPU cores + 1) for optimal throughput.

topics.name: Celery + Redis — Offloading CPU-bound ML Inference to Background Workers
topics.desc: The answer to the 500-concurrent-users scenario below.The architecture — FastAPI receives request → enqueues task in Redis broker → Celery worker process picks it up → runs GPU inference in separate process → result stored in Redis result backend → client polls or gets callback — is a multi-component system that requires seeing the full dataflow diagram. Getting this wrong blocks FastAPI's event loop and causes all requests to time out.

topics.name: Model Loading Strategy — Shared Memory, Forked Workers, Torch.share_memory_()
topics.desc: When a Gunicorn master process forks N worker processes, the naive approach loads the model weights N times. The correct approach loads the model in the master before forking — child processes inherit the weights via OS copy-on-write page sharing. Seeing a memory diagram of forked processes sharing the same physical memory pages is the insight that answers the memory overhead interview scenario.
